newsitem.title: USA: USAir to buy 120 Airbus aircraft.
newsitem.headline: USAir to buy 120 Airbus aircraft.

text.p: USAir Group Inc. said Wednesday it agreed to buy 120 Airbus Industrie aircraft in a deal that could be worth more than $5 billion and took an option to buy as many as 280 additional planes.

The order is a major victory for Airbus, the European consortium, and a blow to Boeing Co., the world's largest aircraft manufacturer, and McDonnell Douglas Corp., whose commercial aircraft business has struggled.
The deal, which will allow USAir to streamline its fleet and reduce costs, includes orders for single-aisle Airbus A319, A320 and A321 models, the airline said.
It gave no indication of the value of the order.
But industry sources put the total cost at $5.3 billion, based on list prices for the aircraft. Airlines often get discounts depending on their orders and relationship with the manufacturer.
Because all three aircraft have the same cockpit, systems and common engine types, USAir said the deal will help cut its operating costs for crew training, scheduling and maintenance.
